meaning: wallet; purse

senses.en: wallet; purse (the small case for money and cards)

examples.en: Have you seen my wallet?
examples.analysis: 钱包 is the object of 看见 'see': 我的钱包 'my wallet', owner + 的 + thing. 了吗 at the end asks whether something has already happened, here whether the other person has seen it.

examples.en: I left my wallet at home.
examples.analysis: 钱包 comes before the verb: in speech the thing you are talking about often goes first. 忘在 + place + 了 = 'left it behind at': 忘 'forget' + 在家里 'at home', so the wallet is still at home.

examples.en: Your new wallet is really nice!
examples.analysis: 新钱包 'new wallet': a one-syllable adjective like 新 usually goes straight before the noun, with no 的. 你的新钱包 is the subject, and 真 + 好看 'really nice-looking' is an everyday compliment.

collocations.en: the wallet is lost; I've lost my wallet

hook: 钱 'money' + 包 'bag': a money bag.

meaning: hundred

senses.en: hundred, after a number: 一百 100, 两百 200, 几百 'a few hundred'

examples.en: Two hundred yuan, OK?
examples.analysis: 百 'hundred' takes a number in front: 两百 '200'. For 200 you hear both 两百 and 二百. 块 is the spoken word for yuan, and 行吗 'is that OK?' turns the price into an offer, as when haggling.

examples.en: My grandpa is almost a hundred.
examples.analysis: Chinese says 一百, with 一, where English says 'a hundred'. 岁 'years old' follows the number. 快…了 = 'almost, about to': he will soon turn 100.

examples.en: It's not expensive, just a few hundred yuan.
examples.analysis: 几百 = 'a few hundred': 几 'a few' fills the number slot before 百, just as 几十 means 'several tens'. 就 'just, only' plays the amount down, which fits 不贵 'not expensive'.

meaning: online; on the internet

senses.en: online, as a place: 在网上买 'buy online'
the internet as a source: 网上说… 'it says online that…'

examples.en: I bought it online.
examples.analysis: 在网上 'online' goes before the verb, like any place phrase: 在 + place + verb. 的 at the end stresses where a past action happened (是…的 with 是 dropped), the natural reply to 'where did you get it?'.

examples.en: It says online that it'll rain today.
examples.analysis: Here 网上 is the subject of 说 'say': 'online says' = 'it says online'. A place can be the source of news like this. 有雨 'there will be rain' needs no word for 'will'.

examples.en: Have a quick look online.
examples.analysis: 在网上 'online' sets where to do it, before the verb 找 'look for'. 一下儿 after the verb makes the request sound quick and light: 'just have a look'.

related.en: to go online; to use the internet

meaning: expensive; (polite) your, in 您贵姓

senses.en: expensive; costly
'your' (honorific), mainly in 您贵姓？ 'May I ask your surname?'; also formal 贵公司 'your company'

examples.en: That's too expensive. How about a hundred?
examples.analysis: 太贵了 'too expensive': 太 + adjective + 了 is the usual way to say 'too…', here as a complaint. 贵 needs no verb 'to be'. Then comes a counter-offer: 一百块行吗 'is 100 OK?'.

examples.en: The food here isn't expensive.
examples.analysis: 贵 is the predicate on its own: subject + 不 + 贵, with no 是 'is'. 这儿的菜 'the food here': the place comes before 的 and the noun, the reverse of English order.

examples.en: Is housing expensive in Beijing?
examples.analysis: 北京的房子 'housing in Beijing' is the subject and 贵 the predicate, with no 是; 吗 makes it a yes/no question. A bare 贵 is normal in a 吗 question, but in a plain statement it implies a contrast (Beijing vs elsewhere), so a neutral statement says 很贵.

meaning: restroom; toilet; washroom

senses.en: restroom; toilet (the polite everyday word, in public places and homes)

examples.en: Excuse me, where's the restroom?
examples.analysis: 洗手间 is the subject, and 在哪儿 asks 'is where?': thing + 在 + place. 请问 'may I ask' opens a polite question to a stranger.

examples.en: Let me just go to the restroom first.
examples.analysis: 洗手间 is where 去 'go' leads, with no word for 'to'. 个 before it is casual and makes the trip sound quick. 先 'first' says you will do this before whatever comes next.

examples.en: Isn't there a restroom here?
examples.analysis: Place + 没有 + thing = 'there is no…'. Adding 吗 makes it a negative question, which shows surprise: the speaker expected there to be one.

related.en: toilet; a plainer, more blunt word

hook: 洗 'wash' + 手 'hand' + 间 'room': a hand-washing room.

meaning: upstairs; on the floor above

senses.en: upstairs; the floor(s) above
楼上的 = the people upstairs: 楼上 + 的 with the noun dropped (楼上的 'the neighbors upstairs')

examples.en: I live right upstairs.
examples.analysis: 楼上 is where the living happens: 住 'live' can take the place right after it (住楼上), or with 在 (住在楼上). 就 'right, just' stresses how close it is.

examples.en: He's upstairs sleeping.
examples.analysis: 在楼上 'upstairs' goes before the verb: 在 + place + verb. 呢 at the end shows the action is going on now, so this answers 'where is he?'.

examples.en: Is anyone upstairs?
examples.analysis: 楼上 opens the sentence as the place, then 有 'there is': place + 有 + thing is how Chinese says 'there is/are…'. 吗 makes it a yes/no question.

collocations.en: the people upstairs; the one upstairs

related.en: above; on top (general position, not a floor of a building)

meaning: a little; a bit; some (also said 一点, without 儿)

senses.en: a little; some, before a noun: 喝一点儿水
a bit more, after an adjective: 慢一点儿 'a bit slower'
with 也/都 + negative: (not) at all: 一点儿也不饿

examples.en: Have some water.
examples.analysis: Verb + 一点儿 + noun = 'a little (of)': 喝一点儿水 'drink some water'. 吧 at the end turns it into a friendly suggestion.

examples.en: Please speak a little more slowly.
examples.analysis: Adjective + 一点儿 = 'a bit more…' compared with now: 慢一点儿 'a bit slower'. For this meaning 一点儿 comes after the adjective; before it (有一点儿慢) it means 'a bit too slow'. 请 + verb makes it a polite request.

examples.en: I'm not hungry at all.
examples.analysis: 一点儿 + 也 + 不 + adjective = 'not at all', literally 'not hungry even a little'. 都 can replace 也 (一点儿都不饿). The pattern goes before the negated word and makes the 'no' stronger.

collocations.en: a bit, slightly (+ adjective, usually something unwelcome: 有一点儿累)

related.en: (after a verb) briefly, for a moment

meaning: to fall ill; to get sick

senses.en: to fall ill; to get sick (生病了 'is sick now')

examples.en: My child is sick, so I'd like to ask for leave.
examples.analysis: 生病 + 了 = 'has fallen ill', so 'is sick now': 了 marks the change. 孩子 needs no 'my' when it is clearly your own child. 请假 'ask for leave' is what follows, said to a boss or teacher.

examples.en: Are you sick?
examples.analysis: 是不是 before the verb checks a guess: the speaker suspects you are ill and asks you to confirm. 生病了 'have fallen ill', with 了 marking the change from well to sick.

examples.en: Put on some more layers. Don't get sick.
examples.analysis: 别 + 生病 + 了 = 'don't get sick': 别 warns against something, and 了 points to the change you want to avoid. 多穿一点儿 'wear a bit more' comes first: a caring line when the weather turns cold.

collocations.en: what illness (does someone have)?; 他生了什么病？ 'What illness does he have?'

related.en: to see a doctor; (of a doctor) to see patients

meaning: had better; it would be best to

senses.en: had better (advice): 你最好去医院
ideally; it would be best if (a wish or preference)

examples.zh: 你最好去医院看一下儿。
examples.en: You'd better go to the hospital and get checked out.
examples.analysis: 最好 goes before the verb phrase and gives advice: 'you'd better…', softer than a command. In 去医院看一下儿, 看 means seeing a doctor, and 一下儿 makes the visit sound brief.

examples.en: We'd better leave a bit earlier.
examples.analysis: 最好 sits after the subject and before the advised action: 早一点儿走 'leave a bit earlier', where adjective + 一点儿 before the verb says how to do it. It suggests the safer plan without insisting.

examples.en: Better not drink tea in the evening.
examples.analysis: 最好 + 别 + verb = 'it's best not to…': advice in the negative. 晚上 'in the evening' opens the sentence to set the time, and no subject is needed for general advice like this.

meaning: country; nation (mostly in words like 中国, 外国, 哪国)

senses.en: country, after 哪 'which': 哪国人 'which nationality'
country; national, inside words: 中国, 外国, 国家, 回国 'go back to one's country'

examples.en: Which country are you from?
examples.analysis: 哪国人 'person of which country' is the usual way to ask about nationality: 哪 'which' + 国 'country' + 人 'person'. The answer puts a country name in the same slot: 我是中国人 'I'm Chinese'.

examples.en: Which country is this food from?
examples.analysis: 哪国 'which country' + 的 + 菜 = 'which country's food'. 国 works after 哪 like this, but as a word on its own for 'a country' people say 国家 (这个国家 'this country').

examples.en: I don't know what country he's from.
examples.analysis: 哪国人 again, now inside a bigger sentence: 哪 'which' + 国 'country' + 人 'person'. The question 他是哪国人 is the object of 我不知道 'I don't know' and keeps direct-question word order. The whole sentence is a statement, so it ends with a full stop, not a question mark.

collocations.en: to go back to one's home country

meaning: to be at home; to be in

senses.en: to be at home; to be in: 你妈妈在家吗？
at home, before another verb: 在家工作 'work from home'

examples.en: Will you be home tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 在家 'be at home' is the whole predicate here; no other verb is needed. 明天 'tomorrow' goes before it, and that time word alone makes it about the future.

examples.en: I'm working from home today.
examples.analysis: Here 在家 comes before another verb and says where it happens: 在家 + 工作 'work at home'. The place goes before the verb, the reverse of English 'work at home'.

examples.en: He's not home. He's gone out.
examples.analysis: 不在家 'not at home': 不 negates 在家 directly. 出去了 'has gone out' explains why, with 了 marking that it has happened. A typical reply when someone calls for a person who is out.

meaning: college; school or faculty within a university; institute

senses.en: school or faculty within a university (医学院 'medical school')
college; institute (a stand-alone school)

measure.note: 一所学院; 个 is also common in speech

examples.en: Where's your school?
examples.analysis: 学院 here most likely means a school within a university. 你们学院 'your school' uses 你们 'you (plural)' because the person belongs to it with others, and needs no 的. Thing + 在哪儿 asks where it is.

examples.zh: 我们学院有很多外国学生。
examples.en: Our school has a lot of international students.
examples.analysis: 我们学院 'our school' is the subject of 有 'have': owner + 有 + 很多 + noun. For an institution you belong to, people usually say 我们 rather than 我的, as in 我们学校.

examples.en: Let's meet at the entrance of the school.
examples.analysis: 学院门口 'the school entrance': place + 门口 needs no 的. 见 'meet, see each other' has no subject, and 吧 makes it a suggestion: 'let's meet at…'.

meaning: milk (cow's milk)

senses.en: milk; cow's milk

measure.note: 一杯牛奶 'a glass of milk'; 瓶 píng for a bottle: 一瓶牛奶

examples.en: I have a glass of milk in the morning.
examples.analysis: 一杯牛奶 'a glass of milk': number + 杯 'cup, glass' + 牛奶. 杯 is the measure word, so there is no word for 'of'. A general time like 早上 with no 了 reads as a habit.

examples.en: We're out of milk.
examples.analysis: Place + 没有 + thing = 'there is no…': 家里没有牛奶 'there's no milk at home'. 了 at the end marks a change: there was milk and now there isn't, so 'we've run out'.

examples.en: Do you want milk in your tea?
examples.analysis: 牛奶 is the object of 放 'put in'. 茶里 'in the tea' comes before the verb as the place, and 要 'want' + 放牛奶 + 吗 asks what the person would like.

meaning: the right side; on the right

senses.en: the right side; on the right: 在右边
to the right of X: X + 右边 (我右边 'on my right')

examples.en: The hospital is just to the right of the intersection.
examples.analysis: 路口右边 'to the right of the intersection': reference point + 右边, with no 的 needed. 在 + place says where something is, and 就 'just, right' tells the listener it is close.

examples.zh: 坐在我右边的是我同学。
examples.en: The person sitting on my right is my classmate.
examples.analysis: 我右边 'on my right': person + 右边. The whole phrase 坐在我右边的 'the one sitting on my right' is the subject, with 的 standing in for 'person'.

examples.en: Is the one on the right yours?
examples.analysis: 右边的 'the one on the right': 右边 + 的 with the noun dropped, since both people can see what is meant. 你的 'yours' works the same way, so the sentence needs no noun at all.

meaning: downstairs; on the floor below; at the foot of the building

senses.en: downstairs; the floor(s) below
the ground floor or street outside a building: 你家楼下

examples.en: I'll wait for you downstairs.
examples.analysis: 在楼下 'downstairs' comes before the verb 等 'wait (for)': 在 + place + verb. No word for 'will' is needed; the context shows it is a plan.

examples.en: I'm downstairs at your place.
examples.analysis: 你家楼下 'downstairs from your home': the ground floor or the street outside the building. 到…了 = 'have arrived (at)'. A typical message from a friend or driver waiting outside an apartment block.

examples.en: How late is the shop downstairs open?
examples.analysis: 楼下的商店 'the shop downstairs': 楼下 + 的 describes the noun, with the place first. 开到几点 'open until what time': 开 'be open' + 到 'until' + 几点 'what time'.

collocations.en: the people downstairs; the one downstairs

related.en: below; underneath (general position, not a floor of a building)

meaning: doorway; entrance; gate

senses.en: doorway; entrance; (at) the door or gate
at the entrance of X: X + 门口 (学校门口)

examples.en: There's someone at the door looking for you.
examples.analysis: 门口 is the place at the start: place + 有 + 人 'there is someone'. Then 找你 'looking for you' says what that person wants; two verb phrases in a row describe one situation.

examples.en: Call me when you get to the entrance.
examples.analysis: 到门口 'get to the entrance' sets the moment, with no word for 'when'. 给我打电话 'call me' is the request itself; the 'you' is dropped, as is usual in requests.

examples.en: Can you get a taxi at the hospital entrance?
examples.analysis: 医院门口 'the hospital entrance': place + 门口 with no 的. The place opens the sentence, then 能 'can' + 打车 'get a taxi' + 吗. No subject is needed, since it means anyone.

collocations.en: at the door; at the entrance

hook: 门 'door' + 口 'opening': the opening of the door.

meaning: to get off work; to finish work

senses.en: to finish work for the day; to get off work
splits around 了: 下了班 'after finishing work'

examples.en: What time do you get off work?
examples.analysis: 几点 'what time' goes before the verb, the normal slot for a time in Chinese. The answer keeps that order: 我六点下班 'I get off at six', where English puts the time last. 下班 'finish work' needs no object.

examples.en: After work I go straight home.
examples.analysis: 下班 splits here: 了 goes between 下 and 班, 'once (I've) finished work'. 就 then links the next action: 'as soon as…, then…', which gives the sense of 'straight home'.

examples.en: I'm not off work yet.
examples.analysis: 还没 + verb + 呢 = 'not yet': 没, not 不, because it is about whether something has happened. 还 gives the 'still, yet' feel, and 呢 at the end signals that the situation is still going on: I'm still at work.

collocations.en: after work; once work is over

related.en: to go to work; to be at work

meaning: to take an exam (in a subject); to test

senses.en: to take an exam (in a subject): 考汉语; also to score on one: 考了九十分
to test, quiz (someone): 老师考我们
to sit the entrance exam for: 考大学

examples.en: What's the exam on tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 考 + school subject = 'have an exam in': 考什么 'the exam is on what?'. No 'we' is said; the context makes clear who is taking it. 明天 'tomorrow' comes first to set the time.

examples.en: What score did you get?
examples.analysis: 考 + 了 + score: 考了多少分 'scored how many points'. 了 marks the exam as done, and 多少分 asks for the number of points.

examples.en: I didn't do well on the last exam.
examples.analysis: 考好 = 'do well on an exam': 考 + 好 'good' as the result. 没 negates the result: I took it but didn't do well. 上次 'last time' sets the time.

collocations.en: didn't do well on the exam

meaning: to have class; to go to class; (of a teacher) to teach a class

senses.en: to have class; to attend class; class starts
(of a teacher) to teach a class
splits around other words: 上什么课, 上汉语课

examples.en: We have class at eight.
examples.analysis: 上课 'have class; class starts'. 八点 'eight o'clock' comes before the verb, the usual place for a time. Among teachers, the same sentence can mean 'we teach at eight'.

examples.en: Class is starting. Stop talking.
examples.analysis: 上课了 'class is starting now': 了 marks the new situation, the teacher's signal. 别…了 = 'stop doing…': 别说话了 'stop talking'.

examples.en: What classes do you have today?
examples.analysis: 上课 is a verb + object pair that can split: the question word goes inside, 上什么课 'have what class'. The answer fills the same slot: 上汉语课 'have Chinese class'.

related.en: to go to school; to be in school

meaning: to get up; to get out of bed

senses.en: to get up; to get out of bed (not just to wake up)

examples.en: I get up at six in the morning.
examples.analysis: Times go before the verb: 早上 'morning' + 六点 'six o'clock' + 起床. A general time like 早上 with no 了 reads as a routine. 起床 means getting out of bed, not just waking up.

examples.en: Time to get up! Hurry up!
examples.analysis: 起床了 with no subject = 'time to get up!': 了 announces a new situation, the classic wake-up call. 快一点儿 'a bit faster' is the everyday 'hurry up'.

examples.en: On Sundays I don't want to get up.
examples.analysis: 不想 + 起床 'don't want to get up': 想 'want to' comes before the verb, and 不 negates the wish. 星期天 'Sunday' opens the sentence as the time frame.

collocations.en: time to get up!; (I'm) up now

related.en: to sleep; to go to bed
